strengths: Practical efficiency contribution: 2-3.5% computational overhead vs. 100%+ for baselines, with competitive hallucination mitigation—meaningful for real-world deployment
Comprehensive experimental validation across three benchmarks (CHAIR, POPE, AMBER), two diverse models (LLaVA-1.5, Qwen2.5-VL), plus MoE architecture (DeepSeekVL2), with consistent improvements
Technically sound approach requiring no additional training or architectural modifications; reuses existing vision tokens as internal reference signals
Thorough reproducibility: detailed algorithm, hyperparameter ranges, official benchmark evaluation, and numerical results with standard deviations
Detailed qualitative analysis with numerical validation (Tables 8-10) showing how vision tokens guide token selection in concrete examples
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (logit-lens, JSD selection from DoLa, vocabulary constraining from CD) applied to vision tokens—incremental contribution
Insufficient design justification: element-wise multiplication (Eq. 8) lacks comparison with alternatives; JSD choice unexplained relative to other divergences; no ablation on refinement mechanisms
Hyperparameter tuning contradicts 'simple' claim: α requires per-task tuning (10^-1 to 10^-6), layer selection differs by model ('last' vs 'all'); no systematic guidance provided
Weak theoretical grounding: circular reasoning for why constraining to top-K extracts visual semantics; claim about vision token semantic content is intuitive but unvalidated
Modest improvements on strong models: Qwen2.5-VL shows 1-2 percentage point gains on some metrics; some baselines underperform greedy on Qwen, raising generalization concerns
Incomplete ablations: no comparison of divergence metrics, refinement strategies, or vocabulary constraint designs; catastrophic failure without subset (Table 4) deserves deeper analysis
Limited failure analysis: acknowledges 'overfitting to visually salient cues' without concrete examples; no systematic study of failure modes or which hallucination types are best mitigated
Scope limitations: evaluation restricted to greedy decoding, 7B models (except one experiment), single LLM family mostly; 'generalizable' claim would require broader validation

strengths: Clear motivation and presentation: Articulates limitations of existing approaches well and provides intuitive rationale for using vision tokens as reference signals
Practical efficiency: Achieves 2-3% inference overhead compared to 100%+ for baselines, making it deployable without retraining
Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Consistent improvements across three benchmarks (CHAIR, POPE, AMBER) and two base models, plus testing on DeepSeekVL2
Well-structured experiments with ablations and detailed case studies (Tables 8-10) that clearly illustrate method mechanics
Plug-and-play inference-time approach requiring no model retraining
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Combines existing techniques (APC vocabulary constraint, logit-lens, JSD, element-wise multiplication) without substantial innovation. Core contribution is primarily engineering rather than methodological

Fundamental disconnect between motivation and method: Section 2.3 motivates approach by showing vision tokens work when constrained to manual semantic subsets, but actual method uses data-driven constraint based on vanilla output distribution—no evidence this captures visual semantics

Insufficient justification for design choices: No ablation on divergence measure (why JSD over KL/Wasserstein?), fusion method (why multiplication over interpolation?), or vocabulary constraint method itself
Hyperparameter sensitivity not addressed: Different layer selections for different models, α ranging 1e-1 to 1e-6 depending on task, with limited guidance for practitioners on new models

Lack of theoretical understanding: No principled justification for why vision token projections combined with model output should improve grounding, or why minimizing JSD is appropriate for selecting 'relevant' visual signals

Evaluation scope limitations: All results on object hallucination only; no evaluation of attribute/relational hallucinations. AMBER results mixed (Cover unchanged on Qwen2.5-VL). Statistical significance not reported
Critical ablation not analyzed: Without vocabulary constraint (Table 4), CHAIRS=0.2 and Recall=0.83 (complete failure). This dramatic collapse indicates potential fragility but is not investigated

Missing ablations and comparisons: No ablation on JSD vs alternatives; no ablation on fusion methods; no comparison with simpler heuristic (just select highest-probability vision token); only 24-image qualitative evaluation

Reproducibility concerns: Hyperparameter selection process unclear ('set for each task'); no code mentioned; different settings per model/task; no guidance for how to determine candidate layers J in practice
Baseline integrity issues: DoLa underperforms greedy on Qwen2.5-VL (unusual); DeepSeekVL2 requires added repetition penalty, suggesting method may have issues with certain architectures

strengths: Clear, well-motivated insight about underutilized visual semantics in vision tokens, with compelling qualitative analysis in Section 2.3
Impressive computational efficiency (2-3% overhead vs. 100% for competing methods) making the approach practically deployable to existing models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three hallucination benchmarks (CHAIR, POPE, AMBER), two distinct LVLM architectures, 27K POPE examples, and MoE models, showing consistent improvements
Thorough ablation study demonstrating necessity of vocabulary constraint and detailed case studies with numerical values
Model-agnostic applicability without requiring retraining or architectural modifications
Clear presentation with well-structured motivation, detailed algorithms, and reproducible experimental setup
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (logit-lens, early exit, contrastive decoding) applied to vision tokens rather than introducing fundamentally new methods

Significant diminishment of improvements on stronger models (1.86% CHAIR improvement on Qwen2.5-VL vs. 5.95% on weaker LLaVA-1.5), suggesting the method may primarily benefit weaker models rather than addressing fundamental grounding
Hyperparameter sensitivity requiring different layer selection per model ('last' vs. 'all') and task-dependent α tuning, with no principled methodology for setting these values
Missing statistical validation: no confidence intervals or significance tests despite improvements of 1-2%; standard deviations only reported for timing
Incomplete design justification: no comparison of alternative divergence metrics for vision token selection (KL, Wasserstein), no ablation on refinement strategy choice (element-wise multiplication)
Narrow experimental scope: limited to greedy decoding, no exploration of beam search/sampling; evaluation focused only on object hallucinations, unclear impact on other VLM capabilities
Vocabulary constraint appears orthogonal to vision token selection; ablation shows severe degradation without constraint but doesn't isolate whether constraint alone suffices
Limited failure case analysis despite acknowledging over-reliance on visual cues; no concrete examples of cases where enhanced grounding hurts non-visual reasoning

strengths: Strong empirical evidence for core claims with systematic analysis of vision token semantics (20× improvement in recall with constrained vocabulary)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks, 7 models, and 3 architectures demonstrating consistent improvements and scalability
Training-free and highly efficient method with minimal computational overhead (+0.6-1.9%) compared to 2× overhead for competing approaches
Thorough ablation studies (Figure 7, Table 10) demonstrating critical importance of vocabulary constraints and robustness to hyperparameter variation
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured motivation that makes the work accessible
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (constrained vocabulary, JSD divergence, element-wise multiplication) are standard; contribution is primarily in application to vision tokens rather than methodological innovation

Hyperparameter tuning contradicts 'training-free' claims: α requires task-specific adjustment and layer selection differs by model, undermining positioning as universal plug-and-play method without guidance for practitioners
Analysis scope restricted to MSCOCO domain (500 images, 62 categories) with single prompt; unclear generalization to medical imaging, documents, charts, or non-English languages

Weak theoretical grounding: lacks principled explanation for why vision tokens encode semantics in text space or why constrained vocabulary recovers this information; primarily empirical without conceptual framework
Statistical rigor concerns: modest improvements (e.g., MMMU +0.74 points) lack significance testing; confidence intervals only in appendices; no power analysis or sample size justification
Incomplete failure analysis: catastrophic collapse without vocabulary constraint shown only qualitatively (Figure 8); missing systematic study of when method fails or hurts performance

Ablation on refinement mechanism incomplete: element-wise multiplication not compared to alternatives (addition, weighted averaging); limited justification for this design choice over other combination methods
Generalization concerns: all evaluations on vision-language tasks; no evaluation on embodied AI, medical imaging, or other multimodal domains; limited testing on older LVLM architectures
